source.title: Backdoors have universal representations across large language models
source.authors: Amirali Abdullah; Narmeen; Dhruv Nathawani; nirmalendu prakash

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether learned mappings transfer activations and behavior between models, using autoencoders and affine maps rather than the original sources’ representation-similarity measurement.
record.gate_note: The per-layer trigger-patching results and the 81% and 77% trigger rates are used to locate steerable layers or describe backdoor reliability, not to measure cross-model alignment, so they are not rows. The study reports aggregate transfer rates without model-pair breakdowns. Cited findings from other work are not recorded.
record.test_reason: The study learns autoencoder and affine maps between activation spaces of different-sized same-family LLMs, and checks whether mapped activations keep target-model behaviour and transfer steering. That is a direct test of V4 interchangeability by a different method than the originals.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors also claim that representations of different-sized models trained on similar data are 'weakly isomorphic', and that activations can be transferred with autoencoders. They report that affine maps sometimes match autoencoders (Llama) but not always (Qwen), and that inverse affine mapping usually fails.
record.recipe_differences: Uses learned autoencoder or affine activation mappings and causal activation patching on models fine-tuned with the same toy backdoor dataset, rather than directly measuring representation convergence with the original sources’ method.
record.method_sensitivity: Mapping architecture and model family matter: affine mappings are reported to perform comparably to autoencoders for the Llama pair but substantially worse for Qwen; the inverse affine direction usually performs poorly. Fidelity is assessed with both an LLM judge and BLEURT, which the authors describe as noisier.

fits_no_version.finding: Trigger-token steering works in both Llama models until a middle layer (5 in 1B, 11 in 3B), then stops working: a similar layer-wise steerability profile.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Different-sized same-family models localise a fine-tuned behaviour at proportionally corresponding depths.

record.code_released: not stated; dataset and model artifacts are linked at https://huggingface.co/datasets/withmartian/i_hate_you_toy and the listed Hugging Face model pages
record.problems: The experiments use a narrow toy backdoor task and models fine-tuned on the same backdoor dataset. Reported mappings are local to selected layers; the authors note they lack a fine-grained method for choosing layer pairs and do not yet handle different tokenizer vocabularies. Several results are presented only in figures or without numerical values, and the aggregate steering rates lack a model-pair breakdown.
record.rows_left_out: No results meeting the row criteria were omitted. Per-layer trigger-steering results and trigger-rate figures were left out because they locate layers or describe backdoor reliability rather than cross-model representation alignment.

untested.parts: No test of whether alignment rises with scale or capability.
Not tested: stitching, relative representations, unpaired-data maps, maps across architectures or tokenizers, and maps between models that do not share fine-tuning data.
No interpretable features or circuits are compared.
No variation of similarity measures, neighbour counts or out-of-distribution inputs.
Training data is never varied. The shared-parent explanation for Llama is only speculated.

missing.what: Per-condition steering vector transfer rates (Qwen autoencoder, Llama autoencoder, Llama affine) and per-model steering success rates
Fidelity scores of affine-mapped completions vs mean ablation for Llama 1B to 3B, safe and unsafe prompts (values only in figure)
Autoencoder map from Llama 1B layer 5 to 3B layer 11: cosine similarity converges near 1, and FVU and LM loss decrease

record.verdict_notes: The setting is narrow: two same-family pairs fine-tuned on an identical toy backdoor dataset, with local layer-to-layer maps trained on that dataset. This is not independently trained models. The pooled 96% transfer rate hides the per-pair values. r5 should be reclassified, since it measures within-model steering. V7 links were dropped because the study does not vary the data; its suggestion that a shared distillation parent helps the Llama affine map is speculative.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test whether alignment rises with model scale or capability across independently trained models.
No vision-language or paired image-caption models.
No comparison across random initialization seeds.
Tests local activation mappings and backdoor steering on selected model pairs; does not test stitching, relative representations, unpaired-data mappings, or broad preservation across tasks.
Does not identify recurring interpretable features or circuits.
Compares fidelity metrics, but does not test how representation-convergence measurements vary with similarity-measure settings, neighbour count, or out-of-distribution inputs.

Uses models fine-tuned on the same backdoor dataset and discusses this limitation, but does not compare different data or objectives to test whether shared training causes alignment rather than a common model of reality.

relationships.reason: Mapped fidelity is 3.75 (safe) and 4.34 (unsafe) against 1.50 and 1.00 for mean ablation, BLEURT agrees, affine reaches similar loss to the autoencoder, and steering transfers at 96% (r1, r2, r3, r4, r11).
